Without it, N = 0 makes the level 0. `B2Deg.deg_eq_one_of_isAlgebraic_adjoin` gives `w.deg = 1` for any field algebraic over K⟮t⟯ with K algebraically closed, with no level assumption. At level 0, jq is in the field: `jqd_mem_full 0 (one_dvd 0)` (NeZero N is omitted there) plus `qExpand_one_apply`. Each generator `coeffEmb (qExpand ℚ d jq)`, d ≥ 1, lies in `modularFunctionFieldBar d`, which is finite over ℚ̄(j) by `finiteDimensional_adjoin_jBar d`. So the generators are algebraic over ℚ̄(j). The elements algebraic over ℚ̄(j) form an intermediate field; its preimage under `coeffEmb` is a subfield containing every generator, hence all of `modularFunctionFieldFull 0`. So `modularFunctionFieldBar 0` is algebraic over ℚ̄(j), every place has degree 1, and degree(single V₂ 1 − single V₁ 1) = 1 − 1 = 0. When N ≠ 0 the existing lemma applies directly.

It is an argument only through the instance-inclusion rule, and nothing in the statement needs q to be prime. If q ≠ 0, then N * q ≠ 0 (with NeZero N) and `deg_eq_one_modularFunctionFieldBar` applies as before. If q = 0, the level N * q is 0, and the same argument as for [NeZero N] gives degree 1 for every place: jq is in `modularFunctionFieldFull 0` via `jqd_mem_full 0 (one_dvd 0)` and `qExpand_one_apply`; each generator is algebraic over ℚ̄(j) by `finiteDimensional_adjoin_jBar d`; and the generic `B2Deg.deg_eq_one_of_isAlgebraic_adjoin` then applies. So the degree of the divisor is 1 − 1 = 0 in every case.
